confidence_notes: I used one web search for food and drink prices. It drew on travel and cost-of-living sites (bookiscout, gotripzi, workation-astro, theworldtravelindex, LifeIndexed). Those sites give beer (0.5 L draft) at about EUR 3.50-5, cappuccino at EUR 2-4.50 (higher on the Riva waterfront), and an inexpensive meal at about EUR 9-11, with konoba dinners at EUR 25-40 per person. I raised these toward the upper middle because July is peak season and many visitors eat and drink in central tourist areas. The search had no clear figures for a mid-range meal for two, cocktails or wine. I based those on the local beer price and on regional pricing for Croatia's coast, so they are less certain. Accommodation figures are general-knowledge estimates for July only, without any search or listing checks. Summer demand in Split pushes room rates far above shoulder-season levels, so the accommodation anchors are the least certain. I converted EUR to USD at about 1.10, the cross rate implied by the RBA's AUD rates.
comparable_city_reasoning: Split is priced like other popular Adriatic coastal cities in July, such as Zadar and Kotor. It is below Dubrovnik and roughly in line with mid-tier Mediterranean destinations in southern Europe after Croatia adopted the euro.
